valuation.method: Bank: tangible book value per common share (TBVPS) projected to the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) x P/TBV. Q3 2026 TBVPS $29.14 (reported 2026-10-14; first quarterly decline in a year on a $3.2B bond/hedge loss from higher rates). Grown about 5%/yr in the base case (adjusted ROTCE 14.9%, less dividends and about $6B/quarter buybacks, plus AOCI drag easing) to roughly $30.5 by Nov 2027. Steady-state check: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(COE - g) = (15% - 4.5%)/(10.5% - 4.5%) = 1.75x, so base uses 1.85x given 2027 NII growth of 8% or more guided on the call. Cross-check: $56.4 is about 10.8x FY2027 EPS of roughly $5.2 (model assumption, in line with Baird's ~10x 2027 EPS framing, not guidance). USD listing, no ADR conversion. Q3 figures are secondary-source (press summaries of the 8-K); verify against the filing.

bear.driver: Credit cycle and further regulatory/legal charges push ROTCE to about 11%, NII growth falls short of 8%, buybacks slow and rate losses keep TBVPS nearly flat.

base.driver: 2027 NII grows about 8% as guided, expenses near $18.5-18.6B per quarter, the $1.2B settlement is one-off, ROTCE about 15%, TBVPS compounding about 5%.

bull.driver: NII growth above 8%, stronger trading and investment banking, benign credit, ROTCE about 17%, faster buybacks and lighter capital rules lift TBVPS growth to about 8%.

valuation.implied_by_close: The close of $51.02 is 1.75x Q3 TBVPS of $29.14 and 1.67x base-case Nov 2027 TBVPS of $30.5. The named-analyst targets average about $62 (range $57-$68), which implies about 2.0x base TBVPS, or TBVPS of about $33.5 at a constant 1.85x.
valuation.sensitivity: 0.1x of P/TBV moves the base target by $3.05 (6.0 pp of price return); $1 of TBVPS moves it by $1.85 (3.6 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted ROTCE (base needs about 15%), TBVPS growth resuming (base needs about 5% y/y) and 2027 NII growth tracking the 8%-or-more guide, with quarterly noninterest expense near $18.5B.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 earnings, expected mid-January 2027 (date not confirmed; check the company IR calendar).

analyst_notes: Five named analysts were sourced from one post-Q3 Benzinga roundup (Oct 15, date inferred from the day after the Oct 14 release); all cut targets by $4-$6 after the $0.91 GAAP / $1.08 adjusted EPS (consensus about $1.10) and the $1.2B regulatory settlement, while keeping Buy-equivalent ratings where stated. Named targets of $57-$68 average about $62, roughly 10% above the $56.4 base case; that is equivalent to about 2.0x versus 1.85x base TBVPS, or TBVPS near $33.5, though the analysts' assumptions are unknown. Horizons are undocumented, so none enter the weighted target, and all calls come from one date, so concentration is high. Baird's upgrade to Outperform ($62) and cuts by Piper Sandler/TD Cowen (attribution conflicts, $60 to $56), Truist, Citi and Freedom Broker lacked a verified analyst name or firm and are omitted; the Fintel consensus on Oct 23 was $63.82.
